target.title: fix(message): ignore populated location on text sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could receive no Telegram reply when a tool-call generator populated the optional `location` object during a normal text or media send. The shared outbound runner rejected the mixed payload with `Location sends cannot be combined with message text or media.`, dropping the otherwise complete user-visible reply.

This occurred repeatedly in a live Telegram session: the assistant had valid completion text, but every delivery attempt failed because an incidental location payload was present.

## Why This Change Was Made

Location remains a standalone send mode when it is the only payload. When explicit text, media, presentation, or interactive content is present, that content now determines the send mode and the conflicting optional location is discarded before dispatch.

This is handled in the shared outbound runner so all message-tool channel adapters receive one unambiguous payload. Location normalization and validation remain unchanged for genuine location-only sends.

## User Impact

Normal text and media replies are delivered instead of disappearing when a model fills an unrelated optional location field. Genuine location-only messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Live before-fix observation (OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.2, Telegram): repeated send attempts failed with:

```text
[tools] message failed: Location sends cannot be combined with message text or media.
```

The same attempts contained a complete non-empty completion message, so the validation error—not content generation or Telegram transport—prevented delivery.

Focused regression test:

```text
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.send-validation.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       30 passed (30)
```

The regression cases verify that:

- a location-only request still produces a send;
- text plus an incidental location produces a text send with no location payload;
- media plus an incidental location produces a media send with no location payload.

Full PR CI for this exact head also passed lint, production/test type checks, QA smoke profiles, channel contract shards, CodeQL security checks, build artifacts, and the repository CI gate. The only failing workflow was the PR-context proof gate because the original description used non-template section names; this body supplies the required authored problem and evidence sections.
